```{r}
get_GOterms_homomods<-function(cat,module,gene_set){
  universe<-annot %>% filter(genes %in% metamorph_orthlist$orths)
  gene_list<-gene_set %>% filter(mod==module) %>% pull(genes)
  genes<-metamorph_orthlist %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% gene_list) %>% pull(orths)
  
  
  params_up<-GSEAGOHyperGParams(name = "GO enrich", 
                             geneSetCollection = gsc,
                             geneIds = genes,
                             universeGeneIds = universe,
                             ontology = cat,
                             pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
                             conditional = F,
                             testDirection = "over")
  
  Over_up<- hyperGTest(params_up)
  Over_up.pv<-pvalues(Over_up)
  pv.fdr<-p.adjust(Over_up.pv,"fdr")
  summary(Over_up) %>% as_tibble() %>% mutate(FDR = pv.fdr[1:nrow(summary(Over_up) %>% as_tibble())]) %>%
    dplyr::select(paste0("GO",cat,"ID"),FDR,Term,Count,Size) %>% filter(FDR<0.05) -> GOenrich_up #Set the cut-off high just to see what possible processes the genes within modules are involved in
  GOenrich_up %>% mutate(mod=module)->GOenrich_up
  
  return(GOenrich_up)
}
```

## Getting ortholog expression matrix {.tabset}
Since the goal of this project is to identify core sets of genes mediating metamophorosis across different species of fish I need to estimate the orthologs between the genes and construct networks of the orthologous genes. For that I need to construct an ortholog gene expression matrix. I estimate orthlogs from OrthoFinder and filter out only the genes families that are present in all 5 species. This step ensures we select gene families that have a common evolutionary history, and not ones that have species-specific evolutionary trajectories (either gains or losses).

```{r}
orth<-readRDS("./04.Orthogroups/Orthologer_latest2.rds") 

rbind(
rbind(
  orth %>% filter(str_detect(orths,"ENSAOCG")),
  orth %>% filter(str_detect(orths,"ENSDARG"))) %>% 
  mutate(orths= str_remove(orths,"\\.[0-9]*")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(Orthogroup,orths,sp),
rbind(
    orth %>% filter(str_detect(orths,"Goby")),
    orth %>% filter(str_detect(orths,"Grouper")),
    orth %>% filter(str_detect(orths,"Manini")))  %>%
  dplyr::select(Orthogroup,orths,sp))->metamorph_orthlist

full_orths<-metamorph_orthlist %>% summarise(n = n(),.by = c(Orthogroup,sp)) %>% summarise(n = n(),.by = c(Orthogroup)) %>% filter(n == 5)

#Get clown orths
left_join(clown$dge_keep$counts %>% as.data.frame() %>% rownames_to_column("orths"),
          metamorph_orthlist %>% filter(str_detect(orths, "ENSAOCG"))) %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% full_orths$Orthogroup) %>% drop_na() %>% distinct(orths,.keep_all = T)->clown_orth_exp

#Get grouper orths
left_join(grouper$dge_keep$counts %>% as.data.frame() %>% rownames_to_column("orths"),
          metamorph_orthlist %>% filter(str_detect(orths, "Grouper"))) %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% full_orths$Orthogroup) %>% drop_na()->grouper_orth_exp

#Get manini orths
left_join(manini$dge_keep$counts %>% as.data.frame() %>% rownames_to_column("orths"),
          metamorph_orthlist %>% filter(str_detect(orths, "Manini"))) %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% full_orths$Orthogroup) %>% drop_na()->manini_orth_exp

#Get goby orths
left_join(goby$dge_keep$counts %>% as.data.frame() %>% rownames_to_column("orths"),
          metamorph_orthlist %>% filter(str_detect(orths, "Goby"))) %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% full_orths$Orthogroup) %>% drop_na()->goby_orth_exp

#Get danio orths
left_join(danio$dge_keep$counts %>% as.data.frame() %>% rownames_to_column("orths"),
          metamorph_orthlist %>% filter(str_detect(orths, "ENSDARG"))) %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% full_orths$Orthogroup) %>% drop_na()->danio_orth_exp

```

### Summarising expression across orthologs
Since there are typically multiple gene copies we decided to use the copy with the highest expression for each orthogroup. Our objective is not to check how individual gene copies are co-expressed (at lease not yet), but rather get insight into the general co-expression of genes with similar functions. In this regard, choosing the gene copy with the highest expression will generally capture the most predominant signal and expression trends. The following piece of code shows that there is almost no difference in general expression trends when representing ortholog expression by using summary measure like mean, median, or summed expression and when selecting the ortholog with the highest expression.

```{r}
#Randomly picks genes with multiple copies and displays summary metrics; users can try other fish and change the higher range of the runif
check_orth_exp_sumarries(exp_dat = clown_orth_exp,
                         a = (clown_orth_exp %>% janitor::get_dupes(Orthogroup) %>% distinct(Orthogroup))[runif(n = 1,min = 1,max =1835),1],
                         b = (clown_orth_exp %>% janitor::get_dupes(Orthogroup) %>% distinct(Orthogroup))[runif(n = 1,min = 1,max =1835),1])
```

### Making ortholog expression matrix
In this step I process the gene expression matrices to obtain a one-to-one (not single copy) orthogroup expression matrix. The expression matrices for each species contain the same orthogroups, hence are symmetrical. They only vary by expression value and developmental stage.
```{r}
#Making ortholog matix
#Clown
clown_orth_exp %>% distinct(orths,.keep_all = T) %>% rowwise(orths) %>% 
           mutate(m=mean(Sample1:Sample21)) %>% ungroup() %>%  
           slice_max(m,by = "Orthogroup") %>% distinct(orths,.keep_all = T) %>% 
  distinct(Orthogroup,.keep_all = T)->clown_orth_exp
cln<-clown_orth_exp %>% dplyr::select(-c(orths,Orthogroup,sp,m)) %>% as.matrix()
colnames(cln)<-paste0(clown$dge_keep$samples$group, rep(".clown",length(clown$dge_keep$samples$group)))
clown_orth_exp_mat<-cbind(orths.clown = clown_orth_exp$orths, Orthogroup = clown_orth_exp$Orthogroup,
                      cln %>% as.data.frame())
#Grouper
grouper_orth_exp %>% distinct(orths,.keep_all = T) %>% rowwise(orths) %>%

  distinct(Orthogroup,.keep_all = T)->grouper_orth_exp
grp<-grouper_orth_exp %>% dplyr::select(-c(orths,Orthogroup,sp,m)) %>% as.matrix()
colnames(grp)<-paste0(grouper$dge_keep$samples$group, rep(".grouper",length(grouper$dge_keep$samples$group)))

                      grp %>% as.data.frame())
#Manini

  distinct(Orthogroup,.keep_all = T)->manini_orth_exp

                      mnn %>% as.data.frame())

#Goby

  distinct(Orthogroup,.keep_all = T)->goby_orth_exp
gbb<-goby_orth_exp %>% dplyr::select(-c(orths,Orthogroup,sp,m)) %>% as.matrix()
colnames(gbb)<-paste0(goby$dge_keep$samples$group, rep(".goby",length(goby$dge_keep$samples$group)))
goby_orth_exp_mat<-cbind(orths.goby = goby_orth_exp$orths, Orthogroup = goby_orth_exp$Orthogroup,
                      gbb %>% as.data.frame())

#Danio
danio_orth_exp %>% distinct(orths,.keep_all = T) %>% rowwise(orths) %>% 
           mutate(m=mean(Sample1:Sample20)) %>% ungroup() %>%

  distinct(Orthogroup,.keep_all = T)->danio_orth_exp
dnr<-danio_orth_exp %>% dplyr::select(-c(orths,Orthogroup,sp,m)) %>% as.matrix()
colnames(dnr)<-paste0(danio$dge_keep$samples$group, rep(".danio",length(danio$dge_keep$samples$group)))
danio_orth_exp_mat<-cbind(orths.danio = danio_orth_exp$orths, Orthogroup = danio_orth_exp$Orthogroup,
                      dnr %>% as.data.frame())

#Use join to avoid non-unique column name and the filter from the above data frames.
purrr::reduce(list(goby_orth_exp_mat %>% dplyr::select(c(Orthogroup,orths.goby)),
                   manini_orth_exp_mat %>% dplyr::select(c(Orthogroup,orths.manini)),
                   grouper_orth_exp_mat %>% dplyr::select(c(Orthogroup,orths.grouper)), 
                   clown_orth_exp_mat %>% dplyr::select(c(Orthogroup,orths.clown)),
                   danio_orth_exp_mat %>% dplyr::select(c(Orthogroup,orths.danio))),
              dplyr::inner_join, by="Orthogroup")->all_exp_orths

goby_orth_exp_mat %>% setNames(make.unique(names(goby_orth_exp_mat))) %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% all_exp_orths$Orthogroup) %>% setNames(names(goby_orth_exp_mat))->goby_all_orth_exp_mat
manini_orth_exp_mat %>% setNames(make.unique(names(manini_orth_exp_mat))) %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% all_exp_orths$Orthogroup) %>% setNames(names(manini_orth_exp_mat))->manini_all_orth_exp_mat
grouper_orth_exp_mat %>% setNames(make.unique(names(grouper_orth_exp_mat))) %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% all_exp_orths$Orthogroup) %>% setNames(names(grouper_orth_exp_mat))->grouper_all_orth_exp_mat
clown_orth_exp_mat %>% setNames(make.unique(names(clown_orth_exp_mat))) %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% all_exp_orths$Orthogroup) %>% setNames(names(clown_orth_exp_mat))->clown_all_orth_exp_mat
danio_orth_exp_mat %>% setNames(make.unique(names(danio_orth_exp_mat))) %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% all_exp_orths$Orthogroup) %>% setNames(names(danio_orth_exp_mat))->danio_all_orth_exp_mat
```

## Orthologus networks {.tabset}
Same as the previous network construction, we first 

### Soft threshold
This step estimates the power to achieve the scale free topology of the data. Choosing a soft threshold power for the developmental time-series data is not straight forward due to the dynamic nature of the gene expression. Therefore, I chose a power that balances the scale free nature of the data and it's mean connectivity to ensure that I don't get too sparse networks. I pick the power that has a scale-free R2 of at least 0.7. While this is not the most idea, since I am going to compare modules downstream to identify homologous modules, I can check for function information from the modules.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
soft_threshold(clown_orth_net_in$wgcna_in)->sft_clown_orth_net#pick 13 
soft_threshold(grouper_orth_net_in$wgcna_in)->sft_grouper_orth_net #pick 13
soft_threshold(goby_orth_net_in$wgcna_in)->sft_goby_orth_net #pick 12
soft_threshold(manini_orth_net_in$wgcna_in)->sft_manini_orth_net #pick 13
soft_threshold(danio_orth_net_in$wgcna_in)->sft_danio_orth_net #pick 13

rbind(sft_clown_orth_net$fitIndices %>% mutate(sp="clown"),
      sft_grouper_orth_net$fitIndices %>% mutate(sp="grouper"),
      sft_goby_orth_net$fitIndices %>% mutate(sp="goby"),
      sft_manini_orth_net$fitIndices %>% mutate(sp="manini"),
      sft_danio_orth_net$fitIndices %>% mutate(sp="danio")) %>% dplyr::select(sp,Power,SFT.R.sq,mean.k.,median.k.,max.k.,Density) %>% filter(SFT.R.sq>0.8 & median.k.>10) %>% view()
```

### Making the networks

This step constructs the network.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
#Clown
wgcna_adjacency(datExpr = clown_orth_net_in$wgcna_in, power = 13)->clown_orth_net

#Grouper
wgcna_adjacency(datExpr = grouper_orth_net_in$wgcna_in, power = 13)->grouper_orth_net

#Goby
wgcna_adjacency(datExpr = goby_orth_net_in$wgcna_in, power = 12)->goby_orth_net

#Manini
wgcna_adjacency(datExpr = manini_orth_net_in$wgcna_in, power = 13)->manini_orth_net

#Danio
wgcna_adjacency(datExpr = danio_orth_net_in$wgcna_in, power = 13)->danio_orth_net

clown_orth_net %>% saveRDS("./02.Gene_expression_and_network/clown_orth_net.rds")
grouper_orth_net %>% saveRDS("./02.Gene_expression_and_network/grouper_orth_net.rds")
goby_orth_net %>% saveRDS("./02.Gene_expression_and_network/goby_orth_net.rds")
manini_orth_net %>% saveRDS("./02.Gene_expression_and_network/manini_orth_net.rds")
danio_orth_net %>% saveRDS("./02.Gene_expression_and_network/danio_orth_net.rds")
```

```{r}
grouper_orth_net<-readRDS("./02.Gene_expression_and_network/grouper_orth_net.rds")
goby_orth_net<-readRDS("./02.Gene_expression_and_network/goby_orth_net.rds")
manini_orth_net<-readRDS("./02.Gene_expression_and_network/manini_orth_net.rds")
danio_orth_net<-readRDS("./02.Gene_expression_and_network/danio_orth_net.rds")
```

### Network stats

We see that the networks have almost the same number of modules. This is expected since the gene expression matrix has same number of orthogroups and the soft thresholds were similar. There is slight variation in the average module size and mean connectivity with zebrafish having the lowest average module size, while clownfish modules have the lowest average connectivity.

```{r}
tibble(Species=c("Clonwfish","Grouper","Goby","Manini","Zebrafish"),
       Number_of_modules=c(length(clown_orth_net$connectivity %>% distinct(module) %>% pull(module)),
                           length(grouper_orth_net$connectivity %>% distinct(module) %>% pull(module)),
                           length(goby_orth_net$connectivity %>% distinct(module) %>% pull(module)),
                           length(manini_orth_net$connectivity %>% distinct(module) %>% pull(module)),
                           length(danio_orth_net$connectivity %>% distinct(module) %>% pull(module))),
       
       Median_module_size=c(clown_orth_net$connectivity %>% summarise(m=n(),.by = "module") %>% pull(m) %>% median(),
                             grouper_orth_net$connectivity %>% summarise(m=n(),.by = "module") %>% pull(m) %>% median(),
                             goby_orth_net$connectivity %>% summarise(m=n(),.by = "module") %>% pull(m) %>% median(),
                             manini_orth_net$connectivity %>% summarise(m=n(),.by = "module") %>% pull(m) %>% median(),
                             danio_orth_net$connectivity %>% summarise(m=n(),.by = "module") %>% pull(m) %>% median()),
       
       Mean_mod_size=c(clown_orth_net$connectivity %>% summarise(m=n(),.by = "module") %>% pull(m) %>% mean() %>% round(),
                             grouper_orth_net$connectivity %>% summarise(m=n(),.by = "module") %>% pull(m) %>% mean() %>% round(),
                             goby_orth_net$connectivity %>% summarise(m=n(),.by = "module") %>% pull(m) %>% mean() %>% round(),
                             manini_orth_net$connectivity %>% summarise(m=n(),.by = "module") %>% pull(m) %>% mean() %>% round(),
                             danio_orth_net$connectivity %>% summarise(m=n(),.by = "module") %>% pull(m) %>% mean()) %>% round(),
       
       Mean_connectivity=c(mean(clown_orth_net$connectivity$degree) %>% round(3),
                           mean(grouper_orth_net$connectivity$degree) %>% round(3),
                           mean(goby_orth_net$connectivity$degree) %>% round(3),
                           mean(manini_orth_net$connectivity$degree) %>% round(3),
                           mean(danio_orth_net$connectivity$degree) %>% round(3))) %>% 
  kableExtra::kbl() %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), 
                            full_width = F, 
                            position = "left")

```

### Orth module heatmaps

Here I make heatmaps to check the expression of the co-expression modules across development. I segregate the modules into three groups with higher expression in the early, mid, and late stages of development.

```{r}
                cols=cols.clown)->clown_orth_heatmap

module_heatmaps(dat=goby_orth_net_in$dge_keep,
                net=goby_orth_net,

module_heatmaps(dat=danio_orth_net_in$dge_keep,
```

## Validating the modules

Here I validate the expression trends of the different modules based on known gene expression trends.

### Eigengene correlation plots

```{r}
#CLownfish
clown_orth_net$MEs->t
expand_grid(c1=names(t), c2=names(t))->df
purrr::map2(.x=df$c1,
            .y=df$c2,
            ~correlation_test(t[[.x]], t[[.y]]) %>% 
              mutate(mod1=.x, mod2=.y)%>% 
              mutate(sig = case_when(
    p_value_adj < 0.05  ~ "Significant",
    p_value_adj > 0.05  ~ "Not significant"))) %>% 
  list_rbind()->clown_ME_corr

clown_ME_corr %>% mutate(mod1=str_remove(clown_ME_corr$mod1, "ME"),
                         mod2=str_remove(clown_ME_corr$mod2, "ME")) %>% 
  mutate(mod1=reorder(mod1, -corr),mod2=reorder(mod2, -corr)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=mod1,y=mod2, fill=corr))+
  geom_tile()+
  scale_y_discrete(position = "right")+
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "grey20",mid = "white",high =  "#e77515",limits=c(-1,1))+
  geom_point(aes(color = sig),alpha=0.5,size=1,shape=8)+
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("white","red3"))+
  theme_linedraw()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=90, hjust=0.90, vjust=0.2))->clown_ME_corr_plot
```

```{r}
three_system_col_plots<-function(orth_net, col){

  orth_net$connectivity %>% dplyr::select(gene,module) %>% 
  filter(gene %in% full_vision_orths$Orthogroup) %>% 
  mutate(sys="vision system") %>% dplyr::count(sys, module) %>% 
  mutate(per_of_gene_set=(n/sum(n))*100) %>% 
  rbind(
    orth_net$connectivity %>% dplyr::select(gene,module) %>% 
      filter(gene %in% full_thyroid_orths$Orthogroup) %>% 
      mutate(sys="thyroid hormone regulation") %>% dplyr::count(sys, module) %>% 
      mutate(per_of_gene_set=(n/sum(n))*100)
  ) %>% 
  rbind(
    orth_net$connectivity %>% dplyr::select(gene,module) %>% 
      filter(gene %in% full_lipid_orths$Orthogroup) %>% 
      mutate(sys="lipid metabolism") %>% dplyr::count(sys, module) %>% 
      mutate(per_of_gene_set=(n/sum(n))*100)
  ) %>% 
  mutate(coexp=case_when(n >= 2 ~"yes", .default = "no")) %>% 
  mutate(module=reorder(module, -per_of_gene_set)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(y=per_of_gene_set, x=module, fill=coexp))+
  facet_wrap(~sys, scales="free", nrow=3)+
  geom_col(color="black", linewidth=0.2, alpha=0.9)+
  geom_text(aes(y=per_of_gene_set-1, label = paste0(round(per_of_gene_set,1),"%")), 
            size=2, color="grey95")+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#25151b",col), name="contains multiple\n system genes")+
  labs(y="Percentage of gene set")+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=90,size=8,hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size=8),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95"))
}


co_occurence_sig_test<-function(orth_net,sys1,sys2){
  
  #co-occurence dataset for system genes that are expressed in the same module
  co_occur_df<-orth_net$connectivity %>% dplyr::select(gene,module) %>% 
    mutate(co_mod=case_when(gene %in% sys1$Orthogroup | 
      gene %in% sys2$Orthogroup ~ "co-occur", 
      .default = "co-occur_not"))
  
  #make an additional random gene set for sanity check
  co_occur_df_random<-orth_net$connectivity %>% dplyr::select(gene,module) %>% 
    mutate(co_mod=case_when(
      gene %in% sample(orth_net$connectivity$gene,length(sys1$Orthogroup)) | 
        gene %in% sample(orth_net$connectivity$gene,length(sys2$Orthogroup)) ~ "co-occur", 
      .default = "co-occur_not"))
  
  #test the target gene sets
  tibble(target_set_pval=
           (fisher.test(table(co_occur_df$module, co_occur_df$co_mod), 
                        simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 5000, alternative = "greater"))$p.value,
         random_set_pval= 
           (fisher.test(table(co_occur_df_random$module, co_occur_df_random$co_mod), 
                        simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 5000, alternative = "greater"))$p.value
) %>% return()

}

rbind(
  co_occurence_sig_test(sys1 = full_thyroid_orths,
                      sys2 = full_vision_orths,
                      orth_net = clown_orth_net) %>% 
    mutate(sp="clownfish", sys="thyroid~vision"),
  co_occurence_sig_test(sys1 = full_thyroid_orths,
                      sys2 = full_vision_orths,
                      orth_net = manini_orth_net) %>% 
    mutate(sp="manini", sys="thyroid~vision"),
  co_occurence_sig_test(sys1 = full_thyroid_orths,
                      sys2 = full_vision_orths,
                      orth_net = goby_orth_net) %>% 
    mutate(sp="goby", sys="thyroid~vision"),
  co_occurence_sig_test(sys1 = full_thyroid_orths,
                      sys2 = full_vision_orths,
                      orth_net = grouper_orth_net) %>% 
    mutate(sp="grouper", sys="thyroid~vision"),
  co_occurence_sig_test(sys1 = full_thyroid_orths,
                      sys2 = full_vision_orths,
                      orth_net = danio_orth_net) %>% 
    mutate(sp="zebrafish", sys="thyroid~vision")
  ) %>% 
  rbind(
  co_occurence_sig_test(sys1 = full_thyroid_orths,
                      sys2 = full_lipid_orths,
                      orth_net = clown_orth_net) %>% 
    mutate(sp="clownfish", sys="thyroid~lipid"),
  co_occurence_sig_test(sys1 = full_thyroid_orths,
                      sys2 = full_lipid_orths,
                      orth_net = manini_orth_net) %>% 
    mutate(sp="manini", sys="thyroid~lipid"),
  co_occurence_sig_test(sys1 = full_thyroid_orths,
                      sys2 = full_lipid_orths,
                      orth_net = goby_orth_net) %>% 
    mutate(sp="goby", sys="thyroid~lipid"),
  co_occurence_sig_test(sys1 = full_thyroid_orths,
                      sys2 = full_lipid_orths,
                      orth_net = grouper_orth_net) %>% 
    mutate(sp="grouper", sys="thyroid~lipid"),
  co_occurence_sig_test(sys1 = full_thyroid_orths,
                      sys2 = full_lipid_orths,
                      orth_net = danio_orth_net) %>% 
    mutate(sp="zebrafish", sys="thyroid~lipid")
  )->co_occurence_tests
```

#### STRING comparison

Overall we observe that a 48% (16/33) of our modules significantly capture known interactions between genes, highlighting the ability of the networks to capture biological signals.

```{r, eval=F}
#Load the data
danio_orth_net<-readRDS("./02.Gene_expression_and_network/danio_orth_net.rds")
orth_danio<-orth %>% filter(sp=="Danio_rerio") %>% mutate(orths=str_remove(orths,"\\.[0-9]"))
orth_danio<-orth_danio %>% mutate(Orthogroup=as.character(orth_danio$Orthogroup))
danio_biomart<-read_csv("./Danio_biomart.csv") %>% 
  dplyr::select(`Gene stable ID`,`Protein stable ID`,`Gene name`, `Gene description`)
#STRING data
string<-read_csv("./7955.protein.links.v12.0.csv")
string<-string %>% mutate(protein1=str_remove(protein1,"7955."), 
                          protein2=str_remove(protein2,"7955."))
#string<-string %>% filter(combined_score >= quantile(string$combined_score, 0.5)) # can try using a score threshold
danio_orth_mods<-left_join(danio_orth_net$connectivity, orth_danio, by=c("gene"="Orthogroup")) %>% 
  left_join(danio_biomart, by=c("orths"="Gene stable ID")) %>% na.omit()

#Make df with STRING data
ppi_mods<-left_join(string,danio_orth_mods, by = c("protein1" = "Protein stable ID"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  dplyr::rename(module.X = module) %>% left_join(danio_orth_mods, by = c("protein2" = "Protein stable ID"),relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
  na.omit() %>% dplyr::rename(module.Y = module)

#Identify intra-module interactions
intra_module_ppis <- ppi_mods %>%
  filter(module.X == module.Y) 
#Count the number of instances of genes co-occuring in the same module
intra_module_ppis_counts<-intra_module_ppis %>%
  dplyr::count(module.X, name = "Num_Interactions") 

total_interactions_per_module <- ppi_mods %>%
  dplyr::count(module.X, name = "Total_Interactions") 

#ppi_mods %>% saveRDS("./02.Gene_expression_and_network/ppi_mods_0.5_score.rds")


intra_module_ppis_counts %>%
  left_join(total_interactions_per_module, by = "module.X") %>%
  mutate(Enrichment_Score = Num_Interactions / Total_Interactions)->intra_module_ppis_summary

danio_orth_net$connectivity  %>% group_by(module) %>% mutate(mean_connectivity=mean(degree)) %>% ungroup() %>% distinct(module, .keep_all = TRUE)->mean_connect

left_join(intra_module_ppis_summary, mean_connect, by=c("module.X"="module"))->ppi_summ_connectivity

#permuted_counts <- replicate(n_permu, {
#make random module assignments  
permute_counts<-function(){
  all_proteins<-danio_orth_mods$`Protein stable ID`
  mod_labs<-danio_orth_mods$module
  shuffled_modules <- sample(danio_orth_mods$module)  
  
  #make a dataset with genes and random module assignments; random version of danio orth mods
  shuffled_df <- tibble(Protein_ID = danio_orth_mods$`Protein stable ID`,
                        Shuffled_Module = shuffled_modules)
  #make the ppi_mods df using the random module assignments
  ppi_shuffled<-left_join(string,shuffled_df, by = c("protein1" = "Protein_ID"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    dplyr::rename(module.X = Shuffled_Module) %>% left_join(shuffled_df, by = c("protein2" = "Protein_ID"),relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
    na.omit() %>% dplyr::rename(module.Y = Shuffled_Module)
  
  #Get intra_module counts;
  #tells us the number of instances of two genes being in the same module,
  #i.e. how often do they interact
  intra_module_ppis_shuffled <- ppi_shuffled %>%
    filter(module.X == module.Y) %>%
    dplyr::count(module.X, name = "Num_Interactions") 
  
  empirical_P<-mean(ppi_shuffled %>%
                      filter(module.X == module.Y) %>%
                      nrow() > 
                      intra_module_ppis %>%
                      filter(module.X == module.Y) %>%
                      nrow())
  #Calculate the empirical_P per module and them summarise them after running the function. 
  left_join(intra_module_ppis_shuffled,intra_module_ppis_counts, by = "module.X") %>% group_by(module.X) %>% summarise(em_p=mean(Num_Interactions.x > Num_Interactions.y)) %>% ungroup() %>% return()
  }

purrr::map(1:1000,~permute_counts()) %>% list_rbind() %>% group_by(module.X) %>% 
  summarise(empirical_P=mean(em_p)) %>% 
  ungroup()->STRING_perm_test_res

STRING_perm_test_res %>% dplyr::count(empirical_P < 0.05)

STRING_perm_test_res %>% saveRDS("./STRING_perm_test_res.rds")
```

```{r,eval=FALSE}
## Module preservation analysis

#For clownfish and grouper

multiExpr = list(clown = list(data = clown_orth_net_in$wgcna_in),

multiColor = list(clown = clown_orth_net$moduleColors$moduleColors, 
                  groper = grouper_orth_net$moduleColors$moduleColors);
```

```{r}
rbind(

mp_plot_clown_ref_goby$dat %>% distinct(mods, .keep_all = T) %>% mutate(comp="Clowfish~Goby"),
mp_plot_clown_ref_manini$dat %>% distinct(mods, .keep_all = T) %>% mutate(comp="Clowfish~Manini"),
mp_plot_clown_ref_danio$dat %>% distinct(mods, .keep_all = T) %>% mutate(comp="Clowfish~Danio"),

mp_plot_grouper_ref_goby$dat %>% distinct(mods, .keep_all = T) %>% mutate(comp="Grouper~Goby"),

mp_plot_goby_ref_manini$dat %>% distinct(mods, .keep_all = T) %>% mutate(comp="Goby~Manini"),
mp_plot_goby_ref_danio$dat %>% distinct(mods, .keep_all = T) %>% mutate(comp="Goby~Danio"),
mp_plot_manini_ref_clown$dat %>% distinct(mods, .keep_all = T) %>% mutate(comp="Manini~Clownfish"),
mp_plot_manini_ref_grouper$dat %>% distinct(mods, .keep_all = T) %>% mutate(comp="Manini~Grouper"),
mp_plot_manini_ref_goby$dat %>% distinct(mods, .keep_all = T) %>% mutate(comp="Manini~Goby"),
mp_plot_manini_ref_danio$dat %>% distinct(mods, .keep_all = T) %>% mutate(comp="Manini~Danio"),
mp_plot_danio_ref_clown$dat %>% distinct(mods, .keep_all = T) %>% mutate(comp="Danio~Clownfish"),

  dplyr::count(pres, comp) %>% 
  mutate(comp=reorder(comp, -n)) %>%  
  ggplot(aes(y=comp, x=n))+
    facet_wrap(~pres)+
  geom_col(aes(fill=pres), color="grey20", linewidth=0.2, position = "stack")+
    geom_text(aes(label=n, x=n-1.2), color="white", size=3)+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#497BB6", "#B6497B", "#7BB649"))+
  labs(x="Comparisons", y="Number of modules")+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(angle=0,size=8,hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size=8),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95"))
```

### Clownfish and goby

```{r}
#clown:317
#Grouper:310
#Goby:363
#Manini:385
#Zebrafish:385

expand_grid(c1=(clown_orth_net$connectivity %>% distinct(module) %>% pull(module)), 
            c2=(goby_orth_net$connectivity %>% distinct(module) %>% pull(module)))->jac_input

# Run the function with the ability to specify net1 and net2
purrr::map2(.x = jac_input$c1, 
            .y = jac_input$c2,  
            ~ get_jaccard_estimate(.x, .y, 
                                   net1 = clown_orth_net$moduleColors, 
                                   net2 = goby_orth_net$moduleColors)) %>% list_rbind() %>% 
  arrange(desc(jaccard_index))->membership_stats

#Reorder colums and adjust the pvalues
membership_stats %>% mutate(col.goby=reorder(c2,-jaccard_index)) %>% 
  mutate(col.clown=reorder(c1,-jaccard_index)) %>% 
  mutate(padj=p.adjust(membership_stats$f.test.pval,"BH"))->membership_stats

#Join with the heatmap data
full_join(mp_plot_clown_ref_goby$dat %>% dplyr::rename(col.clown=mods),
          membership_stats, by = "col.clown",relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(clown.pres=pres, stages.clown=stages, mod.z.clown=mod.z)->membership_stats
#Join with the heatmap data
full_join(mp_plot_goby_ref_clown$dat %>% dplyr::rename(col.goby=mods),
          membership_stats, by = "col.goby",relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(goby.pres=pres, stages.goby=stages, mod.z.goby=mod.z) ->membership_stats

membership_stats %>% dplyr::select(c(col.clown, col.goby, jaccard_index, padj, clown.pres, goby.pres)) %>% 
  mutate(sig_ovelap=case_when(
  padj < 0.05 ~ "yes", padj > 0.05 ~ "no")) %>% mutate(col.clown=reorder(col.clown,-jaccard_index))->membership_stats2

full_join(membership_stats %>% dplyr::select(c(col.clown, col.goby, jaccard_index, padj, clown.pres, goby.pres)) %>%
             mutate(sig_ovelap=case_when(
               padj < 0.05 ~ "yes", padj > 0.05 ~ "no")) %>% mutate(col.clown=reorder(col.clown,-jaccard_index)),
           membership_stats2 %>% filter(sig_ovelap == "yes") %>% 
             mutate(homo=case_when(
               jaccard_index >= quantile(membership_stats$jaccard_index,0.75) & sig_ovelap == "yes" ~ "homologous",
               .default = "non-homologous")) %>% 
     distinct(col.clown,col.goby, .keep_all = T) %>% 
   slice_max(order_by = jaccard_index,by = col.clown,n = 2,) %>% dplyr::select(col.clown,col.goby,homo),by = c("col.clown","col.goby")) %>%
   replace_na(list(homo="non-homologous"))->membership_stats2
  
membership_stats2 %>%  
  ggplot(aes(x=col.goby, y=col.clown))+
  geom_tile(aes(fill=jaccard_index, color=homo, width=0.8, height=0.8), size=0.3)+
  scale_y_discrete(position = "right") +
  facet_grid(clown.pres~goby.pres,space = "free",scales = "free")+
  labs(x=NULL, y=NULL)+
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9,"Oranges"),limits=c(0,0.5))+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("black","white"))+
  ggnewscale::new_scale_color()+
  geom_point(aes(color = sig_ovelap),alpha=0.3,size=0.3,shape=8)+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("white","red3"))+
  theme_void()+
  theme(strip.text = element_blank(),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "left",
        axis.text = element_blank())->p1

  
  membership_stats %>% dplyr::select(c(col.clown, col.goby, jaccard_index, padj, clown.pres, goby.pres,phase.x)) %>% mutate(col.clown=reorder(col.clown,-jaccard_index)) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x=col.goby,y=1))+
    geom_tile(aes(fill=goby.pres))+
    facet_grid(cols = vars(goby.pres),space = "free",scales = "free")+
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#497BB6", "#B6497B", "#7BB649"))+
    ggnewscale::new_scale_fill()+
    geom_tile(aes(fill=phase.x, y=2))+
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#497", "#B64", "#7BB"))+
    labs(x="Goby modules", y=NULL)+
    theme_minimal()+
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = -90,hjust = -0.005,vjust = 0.2),
          strip.text = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "none")->p2
  
  membership_stats %>% dplyr::select(c(col.clown, col.goby, jaccard_index, padj, clown.pres, goby.pres,phase.y)) %>% mutate(col.clown=reorder(col.clown,-jaccard_index)) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(y=col.clown,x=1))+
    facet_grid(rows = vars(clown.pres),space = "free",scales = "free")+
    geom_tile(aes(fill=clown.pres))+
    scale_y_discrete(position = "right") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#497BB6", "#B6497B", "#7BB649"))+
    ggnewscale::new_scale_fill()+
    geom_tile(aes(fill=phase.y, x=0))+
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#497", "#B64", "#7BB"))+
    labs(x=NULL, y="Clownfish modules")+
    theme_minimal()+
    theme(strip.text = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x =  element_blank(),
          legend.position = "none")->p3
  
  qnt<-max(membership_stats$mod.z.clown)
  membership_stats %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = stages.clown,y = col.clown))+
  facet_grid(rows = vars(clown.pres),space = "free",scales = "free")+
  geom_tile(aes(fill = mod.z.clown), color = "grey80",) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colors = rev(cols.clown(11)), limits = c(-qnt, qnt),
                       breaks = c(-qnt, 0, qnt), labels = c(paste0("<", round(-qnt)), "0", paste0(">", round(qnt))))+
  labs(y=NULL, x="Clownfish stages")+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90,hjust = -0.005,vjust = 0.2),
                        strip.text = element_blank(),
                        strip.background = element_blank(),
                        panel.grid = element_blank(),
                        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
                        legend.position = "top")->p4
  
  qnt<-max(membership_stats$mod.z.goby)
  membership_stats %>% 
  ggplot(aes(y = stages.goby,x = col.goby))+
  facet_grid(cols = vars(goby.pres),space = "free",scales = "free")+
  geom_tile(aes(fill = mod.z.goby), color = "grey80",) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colors = rev(cols.goby(11)), limits = c(-qnt, qnt),
                       breaks = c(-qnt, 0, qnt), labels = c(paste0("<", round(-qnt)), "0", paste0(">", round(qnt))))+
  labs(x=NULL, y="Goby stages")+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(strip.text = element_blank(),
                        strip.background = element_blank(),
                        panel.grid = element_blank(),
                        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
                        legend.position = "bottom")->p5
  
  
  
wrap_plots(p1,p3,p2,nrow = 2,ncol = 2, heights = c(1,0.05), widths = c(1, 0.05))->wrapped_plot_clown_goby
```

### Clownfish and manini

```{r}
#clown:317
#Grouper:310
#Goby:363
#Manini:385
#Zebrafish:385

expand_grid(c1=(clown_orth_net$connectivity %>% distinct(module) %>% pull(module)), 
            c2=(manini_orth_net$connectivity %>% distinct(module) %>% pull(module)))->jac_input

# Run the function with the ability to specify net1 and net2
purrr::map2(.x = jac_input$c1, 
            .y = jac_input$c2,  
            ~ get_jaccard_estimate(.x, .y, 
                                   net1 = clown_orth_net$moduleColors, 
                                   net2 = manini_orth_net$moduleColors)) %>% list_rbind() %>% 
  arrange(desc(jaccard_index))->membership_stats

#Reorder colums and adjust the pvalues
membership_stats %>% mutate(col.manini=reorder(c2,-jaccard_index)) %>% 
  mutate(col.clown=reorder(c1,-jaccard_index)) %>% 
  mutate(padj=p.adjust(membership_stats$f.test.pval,"BH"))->membership_stats

#Join with the heatmap data
full_join(mp_plot_clown_ref_manini$dat %>% dplyr::rename(col.clown=mods),
          membership_stats, by = "col.clown",relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(clown.pres=pres, stages.clown=stages, mod.z.clown=mod.z)->membership_stats
#Join with the heatmap data
full_join(mp_plot_manini_ref_clown$dat %>% dplyr::rename(col.manini=mods),
          membership_stats, by = "col.manini",relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(manini.pres=pres, stages.manini=stages, mod.z.manini=mod.z) ->membership_stats


membership_stats %>% dplyr::select(c(col.clown, col.manini, jaccard_index, padj, clown.pres, manini.pres)) %>% 
  mutate(sig_ovelap=case_when(
  padj < 0.05 ~ "yes", padj > 0.05 ~ "no")) %>% mutate(col.clown=reorder(col.clown,-jaccard_index))->membership_stats2

 full_join(membership_stats %>% dplyr::select(c(col.clown, col.manini, jaccard_index, padj, clown.pres, manini.pres)) %>%
             mutate(sig_ovelap=case_when(
               padj < 0.05 ~ "yes", padj > 0.05 ~ "no")) %>% mutate(col.clown=reorder(col.clown,-jaccard_index)),
           membership_stats2 %>% filter(sig_ovelap == "yes") %>% 
             mutate(homo=case_when(
               jaccard_index >= quantile(membership_stats$jaccard_index,0.75) & sig_ovelap == "yes" ~ "homologous",
               .default = "non-homologous")) %>% 
     distinct(col.clown,col.manini, .keep_all = T) %>% 
   slice_max(order_by = jaccard_index,by = col.clown, n=2) %>% dplyr::select(col.clown,col.manini,homo),by = c("col.clown","col.manini")) %>%
   replace_na(list(homo="non-homologous"))->membership_stats2
  
membership_stats2 %>%  
  ggplot(aes(x=col.manini, y=col.clown))+
  geom_tile(aes(fill=jaccard_index, color=homo, width=0.8, height=0.8), size=0.3)+
  scale_y_discrete(position = "right") +
  facet_grid(clown.pres~manini.pres,space = "free",scales = "free")+
  labs(x=NULL, y=NULL)+
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9,"Oranges"),limits=c(0,0.5))+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("black","white"))+
  ggnewscale::new_scale_color()+
  geom_point(aes(color = sig_ovelap),alpha=0.3,size=0.3,shape=8)+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("white","red3"))+
  theme_void()+
  theme(strip.text = element_blank(),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "left",
        axis.text = element_blank())->p1

  
  membership_stats %>% dplyr::select(c(col.clown, col.manini, jaccard_index, padj, clown.pres, manini.pres,phase.x)) %>% mutate(col.clown=reorder(col.clown,-jaccard_index)) %>%

    theme_minimal()+
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = -90,hjust = -0.005,vjust = 0.2),
          strip.text = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "none")->p2
  
  membership_stats %>% dplyr::select(c(col.clown, col.manini, jaccard_index, padj, clown.pres, manini.pres,phase.y)) %>% mutate(col.clown=reorder(col.clown,-jaccard_index)) %>%

    labs(x=NULL, y="Clownfish modules")+
    theme_minimal()+
    theme(strip.text = element_blank(),

          axis.text.x =  element_blank(),
          legend.position = "none")->p3
  
  qnt<-max(membership_stats$mod.z.clown)
```

### Extract homologous modules

Start in sequence with the largest pairs first.

```{r}
#clown:317
#Grouper:310
#Goby:363
#Manini:385
#Zebrafish:385

inner_join(
  wrapped_plot_clown_manini[[1]][1] %>% as.data.frame() %>% filter(data.sig_ovelap == "yes") %>%
    distinct(data.col.clown, data.col.manini, .keep_all = T) %>%
    dplyr::rename(col.clown=data.col.clown, 
                  col.manini=data.col.manini, 
                  jaccard.index.clown.manini=data.jaccard_index, 
                  clown.ref.pres.manini=data.clown.pres, 
                  manini.ref.pres.clown=data.manini.pres),
  
      wrapped_plot_clown_danio[[1]][1] %>% as.data.frame() %>% filter(data.sig_ovelap == "yes") %>% distinct(data.col.clown, data.col.danio, .keep_all = T) %>% 
    dplyr::rename(col.clown=data.col.clown, 
                  col.danio=data.col.danio, 
                  jaccard.index.clown.danio=data.jaccard_index, 
                  clown.ref.pres.danio=data.clown.pres, 
                  danio.ref.pres.clown=data.danio.pres),
 by = "col.clown", relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
  
  inner_join(
     wrapped_plot_clown_goby[[1]][1] %>% as.data.frame() %>% filter(data.sig_ovelap == "yes") %>% 
    distinct(data.col.clown, data.col.goby, .keep_all = T) %>% 
    dplyr::rename(col.clown=data.col.clown, 
                  col.goby=data.col.goby, 
                  jaccard.index.clown.goby=data.jaccard_index, 
                  clown.ref.pres.goby=data.clown.pres, 
                  goby.ref.pres.clown=data.goby.pres),
    by = "col.clown", relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
  
  inner_join(
    wrapped_plot_clown_grouper[[1]][1] %>% as.data.frame() %>% filter(data.sig_ovelap == "yes")
    %>% distinct(data.col.clown, data.col.grouper, .keep_all = T) %>%
      dplyr::rename(col.clown=data.col.clown, 
                  col.grouper=data.col.grouper, 
                  jaccard.index.clown.grouper=data.jaccard_index, 
                  clown.ref.pres.grouper=data.clown.pres, 
                  grouper.ref.pres.clown=data.grouper.pres),
    by = "col.clown", relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
  dplyr::select(c(col.clown,
                  col.goby,
                  col.danio,
                  col.manini,
                  col.grouper,
                  jaccard.index.clown.goby,
                  jaccard.index.clown.danio,
                  jaccard.index.clown.manini,
                  jaccard.index.clown.grouper,
                  clown.ref.pres.goby,
                  clown.ref.pres.danio,
                  clown.ref.pres.manini,
                  clown.ref.pres.grouper,
                  goby.ref.pres.clown,
                  danio.ref.pres.clown,
                  manini.ref.pres.clown,
                  grouper.ref.pres.clown))->homologous_modules

homologous_modules %>% saveRDS("./RDS/homologous_modules.rds")
```

## Extract homologous gene lists
```{r}
#combine all the jaccard similarities
rbind(
tibble(all_jac=homologous_modules$jaccard.index.clown.goby),
tibble(all_jac=homologous_modules$jaccard.index.clown.danio),
tibble(all_jac=homologous_modules$jaccard.index.clown.manini),
tibble(all_jac=homologous_modules$jaccard.index.clown.grouper))->all_jac

#long version of data
homologous_modules %>% pivot_longer(contains("col"), names_to = "species.col", values_to = "col") %>% 
  pivot_longer(contains("jaccard"), names_to = "jaccard.comp", values_to = "jaccard.val") %>% 
  pivot_longer(contains("pres"),names_to = "pres.comp", values_to = "pres.val")->homologous_long

#filter out the top 30% homologous module comparisons
homologous_long %>% filter(jaccard.val >= quantile(all_jac$all_jac,0.70)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(species.col, col) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = species.col, values_from = col) %>% 
  unnest(cols = c(col.goby, col.danio, col.manini, col.grouper, col.clown)) %>% 
  distinct(col.goby, col.danio, col.manini, col.grouper, col.clown)->homologous_filtered

homologous_gene_list<-function(mod){ 
  #this functions takes stable module assignments e.g. from clown and then combines all the other species and collates the data 
  #to obtain lists of genes shared between all 'homologous' modules
  #these genes can be though to represent conserved processes across species
  #annotating them shows which key processes have a high degree of co-regulation among species
  #select one column with stable annotation
  
  #homologous_filtered %>% filter(col.clown==mod)->one_col
  non_homologous_filtered %>% filter(col.clown==mod)->one_col #Use for non-homologus modules

  #get the list of 'homologus' columns in other species
  one_col %>% distinct(col.goby) %>% pull(col.goby)->goby_col_list
  one_col %>% distinct(col.danio) %>% pull(col.danio)->danio_col_list
  one_col %>% distinct(col.manini) %>% pull(col.manini)->manini_col_list
  one_col %>% distinct(col.grouper) %>% pull(col.grouper)->grouper_col_list
  
  #Here I get the genes from the above list of modules
  danio_col_get<-function(c1){danio_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(module==c1) %>% return()}
  
  manini_col_get<-function(c1){manini_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(module==c1) %>% return()}
  
  grouper_col_get<-function(c1){grouper_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(module==c1) %>% return()}
  
  goby_col_get<-function(c1){goby_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(module==c1) %>% return()}
  
  #I then combine all the genes from the list of modules above to select the genes that are present in all the modules. 
  #e.g. The orange clownfish module has significant overlap between darkgrey, tan, and green modules in zebrafish. While in manini, it has significant overlaps between darkturquoise, greenyellow, red, and green modules.
  #I take the genes from the zebrafish set and the manini set and combine them to only include genes that are present in both. I do this for the other two species.
  #The result is a list of genes that are, to an extent, co-expressed together. I say to an extent because, the same gene might not always be co-expressed together in the same module, in all species. 
  #For instance, look at the top ten genes in the common_all object. You'll see that all these genes are expressed together in the darkgrey module in zebrafish, but in manini some are expressed together in the greenyellow module, while some are expressed together in the red, or green module.  Essentially, this filtering approach captures genes that, on an average tend to be co-expressed together. This is expected considering they are different species with different developmental trajectories, but the fact that we can find a large degree of overlap between gene interactions across species highlights the presence of a common regulatory underpinning between orthologs. However, studying the deviations and specific modification of the network in each species will provide valuable information regarding the interplay of gene expression and regulatory evolution. 
  
inner_join(
    purrr::map(danio_col_list,danio_col_get) %>% list_rbind(),
    purrr::map(manini_col_list,manini_col_get) %>% list_rbind(), by = "gene", suffix = c(".danio", ".manini")) %>% 
    inner_join(purrr::map(grouper_col_list,grouper_col_get) %>% list_rbind(), by = "gene") %>% 
    inner_join(purrr::map(goby_col_list,goby_col_get) %>% list_rbind(), by = "gene", suffix = c(".grouper",".goby"))->common_all
  
  tibble(genes=common_all %>% inner_join(clown_orth_net$connectivity, by = "gene") %>% filter(module==mod)  %>% pull(gene)) %>% 
    mutate(mod=mod)%>% return()
  }

cols<-homologous_filtered %>% distinct(col.clown)
purrr::map(cols$col.clown, homologous_gene_list) %>% list_rbind() %>% distinct(genes, .keep_all = T)->homologous_genes
homologous_genes %>% distinct(mod)

homologous_genes %>% saveRDS("./RDS/homologous_genes.rds")

#Non-homologus, low preservation modules
clown_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(!module %in% (homologous_genes %>% distinct(mod) %>% pull(mod))) %>% distinct(module)->non_homologous_mods

homologous_modules %>% filter(col.clown %in% non_homologous_mods$module) %>% pivot_longer(contains("col"), names_to = "species.col", values_to = "col") %>% 
  pivot_longer(contains("jaccard"), names_to = "jaccard.comp", values_to = "jaccard.val") %>% 
  pivot_longer(contains("pres"),names_to = "pres.comp", values_to = "pres.val")->homologous_long_non_homologus

#filter out the top 30% non-homologous module comparisons
homologous_long_non_homologus %>% filter(jaccard.val >= quantile(homologous_long_non_homologus$jaccard.val,0.70)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(species.col, col) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = species.col, values_from =
                                                    col) %>% 
  unnest(cols = c(col.goby, col.danio, col.manini, col.grouper, col.clown)) %>%
  distinct(col.goby, col.danio, col.manini, col.grouper, col.clown)->non_homologous_filtered

cols<-non_homologous_filtered %>% distinct(col.clown)

non_homologous_genes %>% distinct(mod)

non_homologous_genes %>% saveRDS("./RDS/non_homologous_genes.rds")
```

```{r}
  clown_orth_net$connectivity %>% filter(!gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>%

wil_test_boot<-function(dat,species){
  rbind(
    dat$connectivity %>% filter(gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% mutate(type="homologous"),
    dat$connectivity %>% filter(!gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% mutate(type="other") %>% 
      slice_sample(n = 25)
  )->test_dat
  
  
  tibble(p.value=(
    wilcox.test(
      x = test_dat %>% filter(type=="homologous") %>% pull(degree),
      y = test_dat %>% filter(type=="other") %>% pull(degree),
      alternative = "greater")
    )$p.value,
         sp=paste0(species)
  ) %>% return()
}

rbind(
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = clown_orth_net, species = "Clownfish")) %>% 
  list_rbind(),
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = grouper_orth_net, species = "Grouper")) %>% 
  list_rbind(),
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = goby_orth_net, species = "Goby")) %>%
  list_rbind(),
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = manini_orth_net, species = "Manini")) %>% 
  list_rbind(),
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = danio_orth_net, species = "zebrafish")) %>% 
  list_rbind()
)->all_fish_wil_test_res

all_fish_wil_test_res %>% 
  mutate(p.adj=p.adjust(all_fish_wil_test_res$p.value, method = "BH"))


```

### Gene copy-number of homologous genes
Homologous genes are not comprised of gene families that vary copy-number as compared to the full ortholog set. Suggesting that the developmental network likely does not have more redundancy (purely from a genetic perspective) xthan other sets of gene networks.

```{r}
    dplyr::count(Orthogroup)  %>% slice_sample(n=2000) %>% mutate(type="Non-homologous"))->ss_test

wilcox.test(x = ss_test %>% 
              filter(type=="Homologous") %>% pull(n) %>% log2(),
            
            y = ss_test %>% 
              filter(type=="Non-homologous") %>% 
              pull(n) %>% log2(), alternative = "two.sided")

  geom_boxplot(color="black", alpha=0.5, outliers = FALSE)+
```

### SS Dendrogram

In this section I do a semantic similarity analysis between GO terms and then make a dendrogram to visualise their diversity and similarity.
```{r,eval=F}
##Compute SS between terms
SemSim_compute<-function(ensembl,annot,measure, semData){
    expand_grid(c1=annot %>% filter(ENSEMBL==paste0(ensembl)) %>% pull(GO),
                c2=annot %>% filter(ENSEMBL==paste0(ensembl)) %>% pull(GO)) %>% 
      filter(c1 != c2) %>% 
  #Ensure symmetric rows are removed
      rowwise() %>%
      mutate(pair = list(sort(c(c1, c2)))) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      distinct(pair, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
      dplyr::select(-pair)->dat
    
    #Make the function to calculate semantic similarity
    avg_semsim<-function(go1,go2,measure,combine,ensembl){
      goSim(go1, go2, semData=semData, measure=measure)->res
      
      data.frame(GO1=go1,
                 GO2=go2,
                 ss=res,
                 ensembl_id=ensembl)->res_dat
      return(res_dat)
      }
    
    purrr::pmap(list(.x = as.list(dat$c1),
                     .y = as.list(dat$c2)), 
                ~avg_semsim(go1=.x, go2=.y, 
                            ensembl=ensembl, 
                            measure = measure)) %>% list_rbind()->ss_res
    return(ss_res)
}

  # Function to get GO term descriptions
  get_go_description <- function(go_terms) {
    library(GO.db)
    map_chr(go_terms, ~ AnnotationDbi::select(GO.db, keys = .x, columns = "TERM", keytype = "GOID")$TERM[1] %||% NA)
  }
  
  
SemSim_compute_module<-function(mod)
  {
  #To get the graphs for the other categories, replace go_annotations_BP, and drGO_BP
  #Prepare the data that has ensembl ids in each module and the filtered enriched GO tems for that module.
  inner_join(go_annotations_BP,
             danio_homo_mods_proc[[mod]]$result %>% filter(FDR < 0.001) %>% dplyr::select(GOBPID),
             by = c("GO"="GOBPID"))->input_GO
  
  purrr::map(.x=as.list(input_GO$ENSEMBL),
             ~SemSim_compute(ensembl = .x, 
                             annot=input_GO, 
                             semData=drGO_BP, measure="Wang")) %>% list_rbind()->ss_out_conv
 quantile(ss_out_conv$ss, 0.75)->qnt
  
  # Add descriptions to dataframe
 df <- ss_out_conv %>% na.omit() %>% filter(ss >= qnt)
 df %>%  saveRDS(paste0("03.Annotations/",mod,"_SS_graph_data_BP.rds"))
 
 library(enrichplot)
 library(clusterProfiler)

# Make custom enrichResult object
 data.frame(ID=c(df$GO1,df$GO2)) %>% mutate(Description=get_go_description(c(df$GO1,df$GO2)))->t
 inner_join(t,df %>% dplyr::select(GO1,ensembl_id) %>% 
              dplyr::rename("ID"="GO1"), by = "ID",relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
   distinct(ID,ensembl_id, .keep_all = T)->t
 t %>% group_by(ID, Description) %>% mutate(Count=n_distinct(ensembl_id)) %>% ungroup()->t
 t %>% mutate(pvalue=0.05, p.adjust = 0.05) %>% dplyr::rename("geneID"="ensembl_id")->t2
 t2 %>% distinct(ID, .keep_all = T) %>% column_to_rownames("ID") %>%
   mutate(ID=t2 %>% distinct(ID) %>% pull(ID)) %>% 
   dplyr::select(ID, Description, pvalue,p.adjust,geneID,Count)->t2
 
 custom_enrich <- new(
   "enrichResult",
   result = t2 %>% distinct(ID, .keep_all = T),
   organism = "custom",
   keytype = "ENSEMBL",
   ontology = "BP",#Can be kept the same
   gene = unlist(strsplit(t2$geneID, "/")),
   geneSets = list(),
   pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
   pAdjustMethod = "BH")
 
 go_db <- godata('org.Dr.eg.db', ont="BP", computeIC=FALSE)#Change ont for other categories
 sim_matrix <- setReadable(custom_enrich, 'org.Dr.eg.db', 'ENSEMBL')
 sim_matrix <- enrichplot::pairwise_termsim(custom_enrich, semData=go_db, method = "Wang")
 p_sim_matrix<- enrichplot::treeplot(sim_matrix)
 
 dist_matrix <- as.dist(1 - sim_matrix@termsim) 
 hc <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = "complete")
 hc_dendro<-as.dendrogram(hc)
 hc_dendro_data <- ggdendro::dendro_data(hc_dendro,type="rectangle")
 labels_df <- hc_dendro_data$labels
 
 library(ggdendro)
 ggplot(segment(hc_dendro_data)) +
   geom_segment(aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend))+
   geom_text(data = labels_df, 
             aes(x=x, y=y, label=label),
             hjust = 0,vjust = 0.4, size=3)+
   coord_flip()+
   scale_y_reverse(expand = c(0.9, 0))+
   ggsci::scale_color_npg()+
   theme_void() +
   ggtitle(paste0("BP GOterm clustering dendrogram of ",mod," module"))->dendro_plot
 
 return(dendro_plot)

 }
```

## Phylogenomics

In this section I use phylogenetic comparative methods to test for a relationship between changes in copy number between the acanthomorpha radiation and clades predating the radiation. Gene duplication has implication towards the evolution of novelty through processes like neo and subfunctionlisation. Here we test whether there are significant differences in gene copy number of the metamorphosis modules between acanthomorpha and the other clades. We can then study the genes with significant differences to infer how the could contribute to the radiation.\
I first use Pagel's lambda and Bloomberg's K to identify which genes have a significant phylogenetic signal for both measures. Following this, I perform a phylogenetic anova between the acanthomorpha and the other fishes to identify genes that significantly differ in copy number between the two. Before running the phylogenetic anova I remove the lineages that have experiences an additional whole genome duplication. Since these lineages are outside acanthomorpha they would inflate the difference in gene copy without necessarily being related to the species radiation.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
##Tree used for phyloANOVA
left_join(taxa %>% filter(!Family %in% c("Cyprinidae","Cobitidae","Catostomidae","Salmonidae")), 
          tibble(sp=pruned_tree$tip.label),by = "sp")->tips_to_keep
drop.tip(pruned_tree,pruned_tree$tip.label[-match(tips_to_keep$sp, pruned_tree$tip.label)])->no_WGD_tree

#Acanthomorpha
##Non-homologous module
non_homologous_genes<-readRDS("./RDS/non_homologous_genes.rds")
non_homologous_genes %>% distinct(mod) %>% pull(mod)->cols
purrr::map(.x=cols,
           ~complete_phylogenetic_analysis_possibly(gene_list =non_homologous_genes, 
                                           module = .x )) %>% list_rbind()->non_homologous_phylogenetic_res
non_homologous_phylogenetic_res %>% saveRDS("./05.Phylogenomics/non_homologous_phylogenetic_res.rds")

##Homologous module
homologous_genes<-readRDS("./RDS/homologous_genes.rds")
homologous_genes %>% distinct(mod) %>% pull(mod)->cols
purrr::map(.x=cols,
           ~complete_phylogenetic_analysis_possibly(gene_list=homologous_genes, 
                                           module = .x)) %>% list_rbind()->homologous_phylogenetic_res
homologous_phylogenetic_res %>% saveRDS("./05.Phylogenomics/homologous_phylogenetic_res.rds")
```

## CAFE Analysis

I use the birth-and-death model implemented in CAFE5 to further validate the difference in gene copy number observed between acanthomorpha and non-acanthomorpha fishes. I run a base model with a uniform lambda for the entire tree and compare the model fit with a multilamda model where gene familes in acanthomorpha and non-acanthomorpha evolve at different rates.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
non_homologous_genes<-readRDS("./RDS/non_homologous_genes.rds")
homologous_genes<-readRDS("./RDS/homologous_genes.rds")
seq_stats<-read_tsv("./10.HyPhy/seq_dat_clean.tsv") %>% mutate(type=case_when(Orthogroup %in% homologous_genes$genes ~ "Homologous", 
                            .default = "Non homologous"))

#random_non_homologus_genes<-clown_orth_net$connectivity %>% 
#  filter(!gene %in% homologous_genes$genes) %>% 
#    slice_sample(n = 1196) %>% dplyr::rename("genes"="gene","mod"="module")#Random gene set to test specificity of CAFE

#random_non_homologus_genes<-random_non_homologus_genes3

#Make CAFE input
make_cafe_input<-function(genelist, cols){
  specific_module<-genelist %>% filter(mod==cols)
  
  orth_gene_copy %>% filter(sp %in% no_WGD_tree$tip.label) %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% specific_module$genes) %>%
    dplyr::select(-c(Family, Order, SpecCode)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = sp, values_from = no_of_gene_copies) %>%
    replace(is.na(.), 0) %>% mutate(`Family ID`=paste0("OG",Orthogroup), Desc="(null)") %>% 
    dplyr::select(c(Desc, `Family ID`, everything(), -Orthogroup)) %>% 
    write_tsv(paste0("./06.CAFE5/New_random/cafe_input_",cols,".tsv"))#change destination in needed
}

#Use this random data for a null
seq_stats %>% filter(type=="Non homologous") %>% slice_head(n=1175) %>% mutate(mod=paste0("random_mod", rep(1:25, each = 47))) %>% dplyr::rename("genes"="Orthogroup")->random_cafe

random_cafe %>% distinct(mod) %>% pull(mod)->cols
purrr::map(.x = cols, 
           ~make_cafe_input(genelist = random_cafe, cols = .x))

homologous_genes %>% distinct(mod) %>% pull(mod)->cols
purrr::map(.x = cols, 
           ~make_cafe_input(genelist = homologous_genes, cols = .x))

random_non_homologus_genes %>% distinct(mod) %>% pull(mod)->cols
purrr::map(.x = cols, 
           ~make_cafe_input(genelist = random_non_homologus_genes, cols = .x))
```

```{r,message=FALSE}
get_cafe_family_results<-function(cols,type){
  read_table(paste0("./06.CAFE5/",type,"/results_cafe_",cols,"/Multi_lambda_model_1/Base_family_results.txt"),
             skip = 1, col_names= c("genes","pval","is_sig"))->fam
  
  fam %>% mutate(mod=cols,
                 genes=str_remove_all(genes,"OG")) %>% return()
}

get_cafe_model_outputs<-function(cols,type){
  read_table(paste0("./06.CAFE5/",type,"/results_cafe_",cols,"/Base_model/Base_results.txt"),col_names = c("q","w","e","r","t","y"))->b
  
  tibble("neglogL"=b$y[1],
         "lambda1"=b$w[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "lambda2"=b$e[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "model_type"="base")->base_model
  
  read_table(paste0("./06.CAFE5/",type,"/results_cafe_",cols,"/Multi_lambda_model_1/Base_results.txt"),
             col_names=c("q","w","e","r","t","y"))->m1
  
  tibble("neglogL"=m1$y[1],
       "lambda1"=m1$w[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "lambda2"=m1$e[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "model_type"="multi_lambda_1")->multi_1
  
  read_table(paste0("./06.CAFE5/",type,"/results_cafe_",cols,"/Multi_lambda_model_2/Base_results.txt"),
             col_names=c("q","w","e","r","t","y"))->m2
  
  tibble("neglogL"=m2$y[1],
         "lambda1"=m2$w[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "lambda2"=m2$e[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "model_type"="multi_lambda_2")->multi_2
  
  read_table(paste0("./06.CAFE5/",type,"/results_cafe_",cols,"/Multi_lambda_model_3/Base_results.txt"),
           col_names=c("q","w","e","r","t","y"))->m3
  
  tibble("neglogL"=m3$y[1],
         "lambda1"=m3$w[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "lambda2"=m3$e[2] %>% str_remove_all(",") %>% as.numeric(),
         "model_type"="multi_lambda_3")->multi_3
  
 rbind(base_model, multi_1, multi_2, multi_3) %>% mutate(mod=cols) %>% 
    replace(is.na(.), 0) %>% return()

}

  purrr::map2(.x=as.list(unique(cols_h$colours)),
              .y=as.list("test"),
              ~get_cafe_model_outputs(cols = .x, 
                                      type = .y)) %>% 
    list_rbind() %>% 
    mutate(mod_type="Homologous"))->cafe_model_outs
  
  
rbind(
  purrr::map2(.x=as.list(unique(cols_h$colours)),
              .y="test",
              ~get_cafe_family_results(cols = .x,
                                       type = .y)) %>% 
    list_rbind() %>% mutate(mod_type="Homologous") %>% 
    left_join(module_annot,by="mod"),
  
  purrr::map2(.x=as.list(unique(random_cafe$mod)),
            .y="random",
            ~get_cafe_family_results(cols = .x,
                                     type = .y)) %>% 
    list_rbind() %>% mutate(mod_type="Non homologous", annot="random")
)->cafe_genefamily_outs
```

The connectivity of the fast evolving homologous genes estimated by CAFE, is not significantly different from all the other homologous genes. Therefore, the fast evolving genes are not hyper-hubs.

```{r}
wil_test_boot<-function(dat,species){
  rbind(
    dat$connectivity %>% filter(gene %in% (cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(is_sig=="y") %>% pull(genes))) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% mutate(type="homologous"),
    dat$connectivity %>% filter(gene %in% homologous_genes$genes & !gene %in% (cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(is_sig=="y") %>% pull(genes))) %>% dplyr::select(gene, degree) %>% mutate(type="other") %>% 
      slice_sample(n=167)
  )->test_dat
  
  
  tibble(p.value=(
    wilcox.test(
      x = test_dat %>% filter(type=="homologous") %>% pull(degree),
      y = test_dat %>% filter(type=="other") %>% pull(degree),
      alternative = "two.sided")
    )$p.value,
         sp=paste0(species)
  ) %>% return()
}

rbind(
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = clown_orth_net, species = "Clownfish")) %>% 
  list_rbind(),
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = grouper_orth_net, species = "Grouper")) %>% 
  list_rbind(),
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = goby_orth_net, species = "Goby")) %>%
  list_rbind(),
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = manini_orth_net, species = "Manini")) %>% 
  list_rbind(),
purrr::map(1:1000, ~wil_test_boot(dat = danio_orth_net, species = "zebrafish")) %>% 
  list_rbind()
)->all_fish_wil_test_cafe_res

all_fish_wil_test_cafe_res %>% saveRDS("./RDS/all_fish_wil_test_cafe_res.rds")
```

#### Plotting CAFE results

##### Model fit

The plot below shows the negative log-likelihoods for two models implemented in CAFE. The Base model, with a single rate acorss the entire tree, and a multi-lambda model where the acanthomorpha and non-acanthomorpha fish have different rates. For all of the homologous modules, except royalblue, the multi-lambda model is a better fit to the data.

##### Proportion of turnover between homologous and random genes
Doing the test without the re-sampling gives a significant difference in proportions between homologous and non-homologous networks. I perform the re-sampling to ensure there is consistency in the data sampling and results.
```{r}

fisher_boot_test<-function(){
  rbind(
    cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(mod_type=="Homologous") %>% slice_sample(n=500,replace = TRUE),
    cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(mod_type=="Non homologous") %>% slice_sample(n=500,replace = TRUE)) %>% 
    dplyr::count(is_sig, mod_type) %>% 
    pivot_wider(names_from = is_sig, 
                values_from = n, 
                values_fill = 0) %>% dplyr::select(y,n) %>%
    as.matrix() %>% fisher.test()->test_res
  
  tibble(pval=test_res$p.value) %>% return()
}

purrr::map(1:1000, ~fisher_boot_test()) %>% 
  list_rbind() %>% mutate(padj=p.adjust(pval,"BH"))->fisher_boot_test_res

fisher_boot_test_res %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=padj))+
  geom_histogram(bins=100, fill="grey70", color="black", linewidth = 0.2)+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.1, color="red", linetype="dashed")+
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(fisher_boot_test_res$padj), color="blue", linetype="dashed")+
  theme_bw()



cafe_genefamily_outs %>% dplyr::count(mod_type, is_sig)  %>%
  mutate(prop=(n/sum(n))) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=mod_type, y=prop, fill=is_sig)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = "stack") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(y = "Proportion", x = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#B39E88","#4EB5AA"))+
  labs(subtitle = "CAFE5 analysis",x="Gene class", fill="Is significant") +
  theme_bw()
```

##### Expansion and contraction of gene families

Here we plot the relative expansion and contraction of homologous gene families estimated by CAFE. We see that there are different points of expansion/contraction along the tree occurring at different nodes. The highest expansion occurred at the root of teleost as a result of the teleost specific whole genome duplication (3R). The second point of expansion appears at the branch leading to *Danio rerio*. This is signal is likely due to the fact that *Danio rerio* has a large proportion of retained ohnologs from the 3R.\
The expansions and contractions are all significant.

###### Proportion of Ohnologs

Here I look for the proportion of ohnologs in the fast evolving genes estimated from cafe. I use the ohnolog list form zebrafish (<http://ohnologs.curie.fr/>) to cross-reference the zebrafish orthologs in my data and estimate the proportions. I see that a majority (74%) of the genes are not classified as ohnologs. When looking at each module, we see some are comprised of a mix of ohnologs and non-ohnologs, while many contain only non-ohnologs. The cyan module comprises entirely of ohnologs. When looking at the time of duplication I see that a majority of the ohnologs were duplicated during the teleost whole genome duplication.

###### At the tips

Focusing on the changes taking place in the branches leading up to the tips, we observed different degrees of expansion and contraction. At the species level, *Danio rerio* displayed the highest degree of expansion likely due to the high retention of 3R ohnologs. There were species that had only expansion and contractions.\
At the Order level, Perciformes and Syngnathiformes had the highest degrees of expansion/contraction.

```{r}

#Expansion/Contraction per species
  all_tree_dat %>% filter(isSig=="yes" & isTip==TRUE) %>% left_join(taxa, by=c("species"="sp")) %>% 
    mutate(species=str_replace_all(species,pattern = "_",replacement = " ")) %>% 
    dplyr::count(type_of_change, species) %>% 
    mutate(species=reorder(species, -n)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=species, y=n, fill = type_of_change))+
```

Here I check that we're selecting Orthogroups that do not drastically vary in number of gene copies between the homologous network gene set and the random null set. We can check the distributions using a box plot and test for difference in gene copy numbers between the two gene types. Using a bootstrapped Wilcoxon rank sum test we observe no significant difference between the two groups. Therefore the sets of orthogroups we use in the selection analyses are comparable in terms of number of gene copies. 
```{r}
seq_stats<-read_tsv("./10.HyPhy/seq_dat_clean.tsv") %>% mutate(type=case_when(Orthogroup %in% homologous_genes$genes ~ "Homologous", 
                            .default = "Non homologous"))

seq_stats  %>%
    ggplot(aes(x=type, y=log10(number_of_seqs), fill=type))+
    ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(shape=21, color="grey40",alpha=0.5)+
    geom_boxplot(alpha=0.5, outliers = FALSE, fill="grey")+
    labs(subtitle = "Difference in number",
         x=NULL,
         y="log10(number of sequences)")+
    ggsci::scale_fill_bmj()+
    theme_bw()+
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
          axis.title.y = element_text(size=10))->seq_num

wil_test_seq_stats<-function(metric){
  
    wilcox.test(x=seq_stats %>% filter(type=="Homologous") %>% slice_sample(n=200) %>% pull(metric),
                y=seq_stats %>% filter(type=="Non homologous") %>% slice_sample(n=200) %>% pull(metric)
  )->res
    
    tibble(test=metric,
           pval=res$p.value) %>% return()
  }
  
  purrr::map(1:100, ~wil_test_seq_stats(metric = "number_of_seqs")) %>% 
    list_rbind() %>% mutate(padj=p.adjust(pval,"BH"))->wil_test_number_of_genes

  
```

##### Global dN/dS using MG94 model
```{r}
#Parse the JSON file from HyPhy
fitmg94_json_parse<-function(orth) {
  library(jsonlite)
  f<-read_json(paste0("./10.HyPhy/MG94/",orth,"_fitmg94.local.json"))
  
  tibble(
    Orthogroup=orth,
    omega=f$fits$`Standard MG94`$`Rate Distributions`$`non-synonymous/synonymous rate ratio`,
    omega_ci_lb=f$fits$`Standard MG94`$`Confidence Intervals`$`non-synonymous/synonymous rate ratio`$LB,
    omega_ci_ub=f$fits$`Standard MG94`$`Confidence Intervals`$`non-synonymous/synonymous rate ratio`$UB,
    p_val=f$`test results`$`non-synonymous/synonymous rate ratio`$`p-value`,
    lrt=f$`test results`$`non-synonymous/synonymous rate ratio`$LRT)
}

genes_needed<-read_tsv("./00.Sequences/genes_needed.tsv")

rbind(
  homologous_genes$genes %>%
  purrr::map(safely(fitmg94_json_parse)) %>%
  purrr::map("result") %>%       
  compact() %>% 
  list_rbind() %>% mutate(type="Homologous"),
  
  (genes_needed %>% distinct(Orthogroup) %>% 
    filter(!Orthogroup %in% homologous_genes$genes))$Orthogroup %>%
  purrr::map(safely(fitmg94_json_parse)) %>%
  purrr::map("result") %>%       
  compact() %>% 
  list_rbind() %>% mutate(type="Non Homologous")) %>%
      mutate(pval_adj=p.adjust(p_val,method = "BH"))->fitmg94_res

```

###### Distribution of dN/dS between homologous and non-homologous network genes
```{r}
rbind(fitmg94_res %>% filter(pval_adj < 0.05)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=type,y=log2(omega), fill=type))+
  geom_quasirandom(shape=21, alpha=0.7, color="grey20",size=2)+
  geom_boxplot(alpha=0.8, outliers = FALSE, fill="grey90", width=0.4)+
  labs(subtitle = "Global MG94 estimate",
       x=NULL,
       fill="type of gene")+
  ggsci::scale_fill_bmj()+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
```

###### Wilcox rank sum test 
```{r}

test_wil<-function(){
  
  rbind(fitmg94_res %>% filter(pval_adj < 0.05) %>% slice_sample(n=200))->test_dat
  
  wilcox.test(x=test_dat %>% filter(type=="Homologous") %>% pull(omega) %>% log2(),
              y=test_dat %>% filter(type=="Non Homologous") %>% pull(omega) %>% log2(),
              alternative = "two.sided")->wil.res
  
  tibble(pval=wil.res$p.value,
         test=wil.res$alternative) %>% return()
  }


purrr::map(1:100, ~test_wil()) %>% list_rbind() %>% mutate(padj=p.adjust(pval,"BH"))->global_sel_diff

```

##### FUBAR
```{r}
#Parse HyPhy output
list.files("./10.HyPhy/FUBAR/") %>% 
  str_remove_all("_cds_treeinput.fa.FUBAR.json")->og

fubar_json_parse<- function(orth) {
  f<-read_json(paste0("./10.HyPhy/FUBAR/",orth,"_cds_treeinput.fa.FUBAR.json"),
               simplifyVector = )
  headers <- map_chr(f$MLE$headers,1)
  rows <- f$MLE$content$`0`
  rows <- purrr::modify(rows, ~ modify(.x, ~ if (is.null(.x)) 0 else .x))
  sites <- f$`data partitions`$`0`$coverage
  
  purrr::map(.x = rows, 
      ~as_tibble(setNames(as.list(.x), c(headers,"q1","q2")))) %>% list_rbind() %>% 
    mutate(sites=seq(1:length(sites[[1]])),
           Orthogroup=orth) %>% 
    dplyr::select(Orthogroup,sites, everything()) %>% 
    return()
}

rbind(
  homologous_genes$genes %>%
    purrr::map(safely(fubar_json_parse)) %>%
    purrr::map("result") %>%       
    compact() %>% 
    list_rbind() %>% mutate(type="Homologous"),
  
  (genes_needed %>% distinct(Orthogroup) %>% 
     filter(!Orthogroup %in% homologous_genes$genes))$Orthogroup  %>%
    purrr::map(safely(fubar_json_parse)) %>%
    purrr::map("result") %>%       
    compact() %>% 
    list_rbind() %>% mutate(type="Non homologous")
)->fubar_res


fubar_res %>% saveRDS("./RDS/FUBAR_res.rds")

fubar_res %>% mutate(selection=case_when(`Prob[alpha>beta]` > 0.9 ~ "purifying", 
                                            `Prob[alpha<beta]` > 0.9 ~"diversifying",
                                            .default = "low evidence")) %>% 
  dplyr::count(selection,type) %>% mutate(n.per=((n/sum(n))*100) %>% round(2)) %>% 
  mutate(selection=reorder(selection,-n.per)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=selection, y=n.per))+
  geom_col(aes(fill=selection))+
  geom_text(aes(label = n.per, y=n.per+1))+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("#4F868C","grey80","#D92B04"))+
  labs(y="Percentage of sites", x="Selection")+
  theme_bw()->site_freq_non_homol
```

```{r}
fubar_res %>%
```

```{r}
busted_json_parse<- function(orth) {

    list_rbind() %>% 
    mutate(type="Non homologous")
) %>% mutate(p_adj=p.adjust(p_value, "BH"))->busted_res

busted_res %>% saveRDS("./RDS/BUSTED_res.rds")
```

```{r}

busted_res<-readRDS("./RDS/BUSTED_res.rds")

busted_res %>% mutate(is_sig=case_when(p_adj<0.05 ~ "yes",.default = "no")) %>%
  dplyr::count(type, is_sig) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = is_sig,
                                             values_from = n,
                                             values_fill = 0) %>% 
  dplyr::select(yes,no) %>% as.matrix() %>% fisher.test()
  
busted_res %>% mutate(is_sig=case_when(p_adj<0.05 ~ "yes",.default = "no")) %>%
  dplyr::count(type, is_sig)  %>%
  mutate(prop=(n/sum(n))) %>% ungroup() %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=type, y=prop, fill=is_sig)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = "dodge") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(y = "Proportion", x = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#B39E88","#4EB5AA"))+
  labs(subtitle = "BUSTED analysis",x="Gene class", fill="Is significant") +
  theme_bw()
  
```

## PGLMM

In this section I take the rapidly evolving genes estimated from cafe and check whether there is any relationship between copy number, phenotypic traits, and ecological traits. For this I use a phylogenetic generalised linear mixed model implemented in brms.\
Since there are multiple genes in each module, I use phylogenetic PCA scores and estimate correlations between the first two PC axes of the gene count matrix and the trait of interest. I model the PCs of the genes as a multivariate response variable essentially allowing me to test for relationships between gene copy variation and phenotypic trait variation.  
I use data primarily from the FishLife package, with has curated estimates from FishBase. For data on encephalisation coefficient I use data directly from FishBase.  The traits of interest are both categorical and continuous. 

```{r}
shapes_dat<-readRDS("./RDS/shapes_dat.rds")
```


### Maximum age ~ gene copy number
```{r, eval=FLASE}
#log of maximum age (years)
 brms_model_age<-function(col){
   library(brms)
   
   cafe_genefamily_outs<-cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(is_sig=="y" & mod_type=="Homologous")
   #lead the genecopy data
   orth_gene_copy %>% filter(Orthogroup %in% (cafe_genefamily_outs %>% filter(mod==col) %>% 
                                                pull(genes))) %>% 
     filter(sp %in% pglmm_tree$tip.label) %>% 
     dplyr::select(-c(Family, Order, SpecCode)) %>% 
     pivot_wider(names_from = Orthogroup, values_from = no_of_gene_copies) %>% 
     replace(is.na(.), 0) %>% filter(sp %in% shapes_dat$sp)->sp_genes_wide
   #colnames(sp_genes_wide)<-c("sp", paste0("gene",seq(1:(ncol(sp_genes_wide)-1))))
   
   expr_scaled<-sp_genes_wide %>% column_to_rownames("sp")->pca_dat_gene
   scale(pca_dat_gene, center = FALSE,scale = TRUE)->pca_dat_gene
   pca_gene_pca <- phytools::phyl.pca(pglmm_tree, pca_dat_gene, method = "lambda", mode = "corr")
   pca_gene <- as.data.frame(pca_gene_pca$S) %>% dplyr::rename_with(~paste0(.,".cpy")) %>% 
     rownames_to_column("sp")
   
   #Get this data from FishLife
   data(FishBase_and_Morphometrics)
   tibble(log_age=FishBase_and_Morphometrics$Y_ij[,1]) %>%
     mutate(sp=(rownames(FishBase_and_Morphometrics$Y_ij) %>% str_replace_all(" ","_"))) %>%
     drop_na() %>% filter(sp %in% no_WGD_tree$tip.label) %>% 
     summarise(mean_log_age=mean(log_age), .by = "sp")->fishbase_age_dat
   
   #join the datasets
   left_join(pca_gene,fishbase_age_dat) %>% drop_na()->model_dat
   
   #Prune the pglmm tree
   pglmm_tree_fishbase<-drop.tip(pglmm_tree,pglmm_tree$tip.label[-match(model_dat$sp, pglmm_tree$tip.label)])
   is.rooted(pglmm_tree_fishbase)
   is.ultrametric(pglmm_tree_fishbase)
   #Must pass namecheck
   geiger::name.check(pglmm_tree_fishbase,model_dat %>% column_to_rownames("sp"))
   
   #plots to visualise response and predictors
   ggarrange(
     model_dat %>% 
       ggplot(aes(x=PC1.cpy, y=mean_log_age))+
       geom_point(shape=21, fill="#8BAE06", size=3)+
       geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE,colour = "#F0710F",show.legend = TRUE)+
       theme_linedraw(),
     
     model_dat %>% 
       ggplot(aes(x=PC2.cpy, y=mean_log_age))+
       geom_point(shape=21, fill="#8BAE06", size=3)+
       geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE,colour = "#F0710F")+
       theme_linedraw(),
     nrow = 1, ncol = 2)->age_plots
   
   #Phylogenetic covariance matrix
   A<-MCMCglmm::inverseA(pglmm_tree_fishbase,scale = TRUE,nodes = "TIPS")
   A<-A$Ainv
   #Priors
   priors_age<-get_prior(mean_log_age ~  
                           PC1.cpy + PC2.cpy +(1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),  
                           data = model_dat,
                           data2   = list(A = A),
                           family = gaussian())
   #Model
   model_brms_age <- brm(mean_log_age ~  PC1.cpy + PC2.cpy +(1 |gr(sp, cov = A)),
     data = model_dat,
     data2   = list(A = A),
     prior = priors_age,
     family = gaussian(),
     chains = 4, 
     cores = 4,
     iter = 5000, 
     warmup = 1000,
     backend = "cmdstanr",
     control = list(adapt_delta=0.999, max_treedepth = 12)
   )
   
   
   return(list(pca_gene_pca=pca_gene_pca,
               age_plots=age_plots,
               model_brms_age=model_brms_age))
 }
 
 cafe_cols<-cafe_sig %>% filter(is_sig=="y" & mod_type=="Homologous") %>% 
   janitor::get_dupes(mod) %>% distinct(mod) %>% pull(mod)
 purrr::map(cafe_cols, brms_model_age)->model_age
 names(model_age)<-cafe_cols
 model_age %>% saveRDS("./RDS/model_age.rds")
```
